American closed models vs Chinese open models is becoming a problem.
items.summary: The work I do involves customers that are sensitive to nation state politics. We cannot and do not use cloud API services for AI because the data must not leak. Ever. As a result we use open models in closed environments. The problem is that my customers don’t want Chinese models. “National security risk”. But the only recent semi-capable model we have from the US is gpt-oss-120b, which is far behind modern LLMs like GLM, MiniMax, etc. So we are in a bind: use an older, less capable model and slowly fall further and further behind the curve, or... what? I suspect this is why Hegseth is pressuring Anthropic: the DoD needs offline AI for awful purposes and wants Anthropic to give it to them. B

items.summary: Researchers have developed Random Network Distillation (RND), a prediction-based technique designed to motivate reinforcement learning agents to explore their environments by fostering curiosity. items.title: Improving mathematical reasoning with process supervision
items.summary: A new approach in training mathematical problem-solving models involves rewarding each correct reasoning step, known as process supervision, rather than only the final correct answer. This method not only improves performance but also aligns the model's reasoning process with human-endorsed chains of thought.

items.title: Building an early warning system for LLM-aided biological threat creation
items.summary: Researchers are developing a framework to assess the potential risk of large language models (LLMs) like GPT-4 being used to assist in creating biological threats. An evaluation involving biology experts and students indicated that GPT-4 offers only a slight improvement in accuracy for biological threat creation, which is not significant enough to draw definitive conclusions. This work serves as an initial step for ongoing research and discussions within the community.

items.title: AI and compute
items.summary: We’re releasing an analysis showing that since 2012, the amount of compute used in the largest AI training runs has been increasing exponentially with a 3.4-month doubling time (by comparison, Moore’s Law had a 2-year doubling period)[^footnote-correction]. Since 2012, this metric has grown by more than 300,000x (a 2-year doubling period would yield only a 7x increase). Improvements in compute have been a key component of AI progress, so as long as this trend continues, it’s worth preparing for the implications of systems far outside today’s capabilities.

items.title: More on Dota 2
items.summary: Our Dota 2 result shows that self-play can catapult the performance of machine learning systems from far below human level to superhuman, given sufficient compute. In the span of a month, our system went from barely matching a high-ranked player to beating the top pros and has continued to improve since then. Supervised deep learning systems can only be as good as their training datasets, but in self-play systems, the available data improves automatically as the agent gets better.

items.title: Competitive self-play
items.summary: We’ve found that self-play allows simulated AIs to discover physical skills like tackling, ducking, faking, kicking, catching, and diving for the ball, without explicitly designing an environment with these skills in mind. Self-play ensures that the environment is always the right difficulty for an AI to improve. Taken alongside our Dota 2 self-play results, we have increasing confidence that self-play will be a core part of powerful AI systems in the future.
